I can reproduce the same state-propagation issue with a provider timeout on OpenCode 1.18.14.

The child session records:

```text
UnknownError: The operation timed out.
```

However, the parent Task tool returns:

```xml
<task id="[redacted]" state="completed">
  <task_result></task_result>
</task>
```

As a result, the orchestrator treats the task as successfully completed, does not retry it, and may create a fresh child session without the previous context. In this reproduction, the failing provider request timed out after exactly `240000 ms`.

Expected behavior: propagate the child error as `state="error"` with `<task_error>`, while preserving the child session ID and enough error metadata for an explicit retry/resume.

All session, message, call, filesystem, provider endpoint, project, and business identifiers have been omitted or redacted.

Still reproducible on **1.18.14** (desktop, Electron build) on Windows 11, upgrading from a ~Feb 2026 version.

Diagnostics from the exported debug bundle:

- `renderer.log`: `fatal renderer error: Error: no such column: name` (at `oc://renderer/index.html`)
- `utility.log`: `sidecar exited { code: 1 }` — the server process dies immediately on startup, so the renderer has no backend
- `main.log`: gets as far as `spawning sidecar` / `awaiting server ready`, then nothing

State of the old database (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`):

- `__drizzle_migrations` contains only **3 rows**, latest `created_at` = 2026-02-13
- `migration` table is empty
- So the migration path from that era's schema to current appears to be broken — the server queries a `name` column that doesn't exist yet and exits

Workaround that worked: delete (or rename) `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` and let the app recreate it on next launch. Session history is lost unless manually migrated via the SQL steps above.

Happy to provide the full debug zip if useful.

Hi, we hit exactly the same root cause and found a reliable workaround.

**Environment**: Taiwan academic network (TANet) — IPv6 is half-broken; Router Advertisement periodically announces a default IPv6 route that silently blackholes packets (packets are dropped, not rejected).

**Symptom**: Python-based clients (OpenAI SDK/urllib, RFC 6724 IPv6-first) connect to opencode.ai over IPv6 → TCP SYN retries until ~125s timeout. curl/browsers are fine (Happy Eyeballs / IPv4-first). In our case the blackhole IPv6 route only appears intermittently (RA lifecycle), so the issue came and went — very confusing until we correlated it with `ip -6 route show default`.

**Workaround (client-side, permanent)** — pin opencode.ai to IPv4 in `/etc/hosts`:

```
172.65.90.20 opencode.ai
172.65.90.21 opencode.ai
172.65.90.22 opencode.ai
172.65.90.23 opencode.ai
104.20.32.17 api.opencode.ai
172.66.173.149 api.opencode.ai
```

After pinning: 100K-token context calls went from ~125s to ~5-8s.

Root cause is upstream DNS returning AAAA records on broken-IPv6 networks — a Happy Eyeballs (RFC 8305) fix in the client would solve it for everyone, but the hosts pin works today.

Additional Windows evidence from a large physical-copy installation (not symlinks):

- OpenCode 1.14.48
- `~/.claude/skills`: 351 `SKILL.md` files
- `~/.agents/skills`: 398 `SKILL.md` files
- 342 identical relative paths across both roots
- 28 repeated nested `skill-name/skill-name/SKILL.md` layouts in each root
- one startup log emitted 394 `duplicate skill name` warnings and ended with 331 unique skills
- neither root is a symlink; matching paths are separate physical files

This supports the issue's two underlying concerns beyond the symlink case: both global roots are scanned, and duplicate-name resolution needs deterministic source precedence rather than concurrent last-writer behavior. A bounded-warning policy would also keep real diagnostics visible at this scale.

I have not removed either tree because they serve different clients; a safe local migration needs one declared canonical owner plus client adapters. Upstream realpath/content dedup and deterministic root precedence would avoid forcing users to break another client's native discovery.

A distinct corruption shape reproduced on Windows with OpenCode 1.14.48. This is older than current, so I am not claiming it reproduces on the latest release, but it strengthens the case for parse-failure recovery and atomic/truncating writes.

Sanitized evidence:

- `~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json`: 169 bytes
- valid JSON document ends at byte 153
- exactly 16 trailing NUL bytes follow it
- the full file fails with `JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token '\u0000'`
- removing only those trailing NULs in memory parses and matches the expected `McpAuth.Entry` shape
- `opencode --pure mcp list` fails before repair, so external plugins are not causal
- only this file was NUL-positive across 213 focused JSON/JSONC config/state candidates

The shared read path is `McpAuth.all()` → `AppFileSystem.readJson()` → `JSON.parse()`. The parse failure escaped as a fatal Effect defect instead of a recoverable bad-store diagnostic.

A targeted local repair preserved a backup, atomically replaced the file with its already-valid 153-byte prefix, and retained the existing OAuth client metadata. Afterward:

- JSON parse passed
- NUL count was zero
- `opencode --pure mcp list` exited successfully and listed the connected server

Useful regression coverage would include valid JSON plus trailing NULs, malformed-store recovery from `McpAuth.all()`, and a shorter-over-longer write test asserting the exact new file length. Deleting all OpenCode state or reinstalling was not necessary.

## Additional Jetsam evidence + workaround

Hit the same class of failure on macOS (128 GB) on 2026-08-06:

- long multi-step local-model session
- single user message ~**136 MB** almost entirely `info.summary.diffs` (included a vendored `.node-runtime/` tree that was not gitignored)
- that session alone ~**6.2 GB** of `message.updated.1` rows (47 events >100 MB)
- `opencode` RSS ~**87 GiB** → Jetsam; Electron renderer for the UI shell also climbed to ~5–8 GiB
- disk-write diag: opencode dirtied ~34 GB via SQLite WAL checkpoint

Canonical `part` rows for the same session were only ~7.5 MB — so this is **summary.diffs × append-only event fanout**, not tool-output.

### Local workaround (plugin, not a core fix)

https://github.com/KirillDeviatka/opencode-session-diff-spill

Caps/denies vendor+huge diffs in `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, spills fat `message.updated` payloads, plus an offline DB sanitizer. **Cannot** stop `SessionSummary` write-path or durable event encode — that still needs engine changes (bound `computeDiff`/`diffFull`, and omit full `summary.diffs` from durable `message.updated.1`).

Happy to test a PR against this session shape if useful.

**Confirmed on macOS (M1 Pro, 16GB): forcing `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` drops GPU usage to near-zero immediately.** Repro: OpenCode Desktop with active sessions → DevTools → Rendering tab → "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce". **Workaround that worked for me (Windows, opencode desktop 1.18.14):**

I was hitting the same "List files failed" / "Unexpected server error" on Windows. The fix turned out to be embarrassingly simple: I just moved the project from a non-ASCII parent directory (path contained Chinese characters) to a pure-ASCII root like `C:\projects\xxx\`. No code changes, no state reset, no version downgrade needed.

This matches @GrayXDD's NFD/NFC analysis above. The server queries lstat in NFD but NTFS returns NFC -> ENOENT -> wrapped as HTTP 500. Until the upstream fix lands, **keep project paths pure ASCII on Windows** is the most reliable workaround. I tried all the "official" suggestions (clearing `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\`, downgrading to 1.18.13, blocking the updater via hosts) -- none of those addressed the actual bug.
